newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: ASIAN EXOTICS - Regionals under pressure.
newsitem.headline: ASIAN EXOTICS - Regionals under pressure.

text.p: * Malaysian ringgit fails to gain much from weekend news of May trade surplus, market eyes 2.5250 level where central bank intervention is expected.
* Thai baht subdued but expected to remain under pressure after de facto devaluation last week.
* Indonesian rupiah firms amid tighter liquidity, speculation of band widening recedes.
* Singapore dollar remains weak on U.S. fund demand for dollars.
The Malaysian ringgit remained under pressure on continued fund demand for the dollar on Monday despite news at the weekend of a trade surplus in May.
Malaysian Finance Minister Anwar Ibrahim said on Saturday Malaysia had posted a 156.8 million ringgit surplus for May, compared with a 2.12 billion ringgit deficit in April.
Dealers said the ringgit firmed to 2.5220 in Sydney trade but failed to sustain its gains as funds remained keen to buy the dollar.
However, the ringgit's downside was cushioned by talk Bank Negara Malaysia was waiting to sell the dollar at 2.5250, the level at which it aggressively defended the ringgit recently.
"I think Negara is still there at 2.5250. That's why we are seeing a lot of selling (of dollar/ringgit) at just below that level," a dealer with a Malaysian bank said.
Banking sources said the central bank had sold around $400 million last week to defend the ringgit.
On Friday, the ringgit weakened on rumours Bank Negara would be holding meetings with local bank heads to discuss possible restrictions on ringgit lending to offshore players.
But banking sources said there was no such meeting.
The ringgit was quoted at 2.5240/50 to the dollar at 0425 GMT against its close at 2.5244/54 in Kuala Lumpur on Friday.
Dealers said the ringgit was expected to remain under pressure from offshore dollar bids with stop-loss sales seen above the 2.5270 level.
But they said its fall would be limited by central bank intervention and corporate selling of the dollar out of Kuala Lumpur.
Elsewhere, the Thai baht was relatively subdued but still weak following the country's move to a managed float exchange rate system last week.
The Bank of Thailand set the reference rate, which is the average of interbank trade from the previous day, at 28.578 per dollar compared with 28.189 on Friday.
"There was some commercial buying of the dollar at around 28.90, but in small amounts. There were no big activities among interbank players," a European bank dealer in Bangkok said.
"There's not much business going on. The spread has narrowed quite a bit in the broker market," a U.S. bank dealer in Singapore said.
He said the continued existence of a two-tier onshore and offshore baht market was limiting interest in the baht but added that the currency showed further downside potential.

"There are still people who are long baht and short dollars, especially Japanese funds who have been holding big positions for a long time. They will have to unwind these positions and that could put some upward pressure on the dollar," he said.
In Indonesia, the rupiah gained from tighter money market liquidity while speculation of a band widening receded.
A European bank dealer in Jakarta said the jump in overnight rates on Friday seemed to unsettle some small banks, which boosted their rupiah reserves and kept overnight money at 14.5 percent.
Overnight money soared to a high of 45 percent before settling at 40 percent late on Friday. Dealers said the jump was technical and not due to fundamental changes.

The European bank dealer said talk of a band widening, which was the focus late last week, seemed to fade as local operators were not convinced the central bank would soon move to widen the band from the current eight percent.
He said offshore players were keeping some pressure on the dollar, but the currency edged up after Jakarta opened.
Spot rupiah was at 2,430.00/31.00 at 0425 GMT against an opening of 2,429.80/30.50.
Operators were also awaiting the announcement of an economic deregulation package, which might give some stimulus to the stock market, in turn supporting the rupiah.
The Singapore dollar continued to bow to fund demand for the U.S. dollar after falling sharply in London markets on Friday, dealers said.
"I didn't see any special reasons for the buying of dollar/Sing in London but it went as high as 1.4380," the U.S. bank dealer said.
He said the market seemed short of dollars, which would keep dollar/Sing supported around 1.4350 for the day while its upside was likely to be capped at 1.4380 for the time being.
The Sing dollar was quoted at 1.4358/68 to the U.S. dollar at 0425 GMT.
-- Syed Azman in Kuala Lumpur (603-206 2323), Mantik Kusjanto in Jakarta (6221 384-6364), Anuchit Nguyen in Bangkok (662) 652-0642 and Sonali Desai in Singapore (65-8703090)
